articles.title: The First Time Producers Had to Find a New James Bond, the Result Was the Best 007 Movie Ever
articles.summary: As the makers of the next James Bond film zero in on their Agent 007, we look back at "On Her Majesty's Secret Service," which replaced Sean Connery with unknown George Lazenby and became a favorite of filmmakers like Christopher Nolan and Steven Soderbergh.
articles.content: When long-time producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael Wilson stepped away from the James Bond franchise last year and Daniel Craig made it clear that he was finished playing agent 007, new producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman were faced with an unenviable task: finding a new actor to step into one of the most iconic roles in all of cinema. In the last few weeks, it’s been reported that Pascal, Heyman, and new Bond director Denis Villeneuve have zeroed in on a few final contenders including Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, and Josh O’Connor. Whoever the filmmakers choose, it’s likely to be controversial; Bond fans are very loyal to their particular favorites, and have been ever since Sean Connery was first replaced in the role back in 1969. The general consensus seems to be that Connery was the best Bond (though Craig runs a close second in most polls), but often one’s preference depends on which Bond was one’s first; as someone who grew up with Roger Moore, he’s always been my favorite, and I argued for his supremacy in an earlier IndieWire piece . articles.title: ‘The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins’ Is the Funniest Series of the Year
articles.summary: In an era filled with too many forgettable revivals and too few legitimate comedies, the "30 Rock" team made something new while adhering to their joke-dense, pop-culture savvy, and network-friendly approach to sitcoms. The result? The year's funniest show.
articles.content: When I first thought, “Is ‘The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins’ the funniest show on television?”, I worried saying as much would be damning the uproarious NBC sitcom with faint praise. After all, the modern TV landscape is awash with crime shows, genre mash-ups, and I.P. brand extensions. Bad comedies abound (and tend to be mercifully easy to spot), but great ones? Hmm. At least the most recent Emmy winner for Best Comedy Series is an actual comedy , but the nominees (including a feel-good weeper , a rom-com heavy on the rom , and that cooking drama ) were still emblematic of a Hollywood era when laughs aren’t the top priority. Turns out, quite a few. “Adults” jumps to mind among recent releases for its successful Season 2 evolution into a hang-worthy Gen-Z hangout sitcom. “Colin From Accounts” capped a three-year run that saw the Aussie romantic-comedy get stronger every season. “Youth” has Sharon Horgan back at the top of her game (let’s not speak of “Bad Sisters” Season 2), and “The Comeback” did the impossible by delivering a worthy successor to one of HBO’s greatest-ever TV seasons. Then there’s trusty comedy staples like “It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia” and “Abbott Elementary,” which don’t need another crossover to keep us laughing, as well as the half-comedies that feel full to anyone with the same funny bone, like “The Lowdown” (a noir comedy), “The Audacity” (a black-comic drama), and “Trying” (a family comedy). Gavin Newsom Proposes Expanding California's Movie and TV Tax Credit to at Least $1 Billion
articles.content: California Gov. Gavin Newsom , on the eve of the 2026 midterm elections, is calling for another major expansion of the state’s film and TV tax credit program. Newsom is proposing an increase to California’s entertainment production incentive program from $750 million in annual tax credits to at least $1 billion, expanding what the governor’s office touts as already the largest capped film and TV tax credit in the U.S. Related Stories Original 'Hunger Games' Star Elizabeth Banks Praises ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ as 'Amazing': Joseph Zada Is a 'Perfect' Haymitch The proposed expansion, announced Monday, would include credits for above-the-line talent, to cover spending on actors’ salaries; $100 million earmarked for independent productions; rewards for companies that commit to more than one production in California; and an extension of the tax credit through 2040. Newsom’s term expires on Jan. 4, so the work of carrying through on any such proposal will be left to his successor. Xavier Becerra, the Democratic nominee, has promised to enhance the existing tax credit but has been vague about what enhancements he would support. Many industry stakeholders are pushing for an unlimited tax credit, but Becerra has not committed to that. At a hearing last week, a California State Assembly committee discussed measures including eliminating the $750 million cap, allowing above-the-line expenses, expanding eligibility and extending the sunset date. The committee also heard testimony from union leaders and a Motion Picture Association representative, who argued that California must do more to make its incentive program competitive with other states. In his statement, Newsom reiterated his call for Congress to pass the federal Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act (MPTERA) by the end of 2026. The legislation — which has bipartisan support — would establish a 20% base tax credit for qualifying film, television and VFX projects that are produced in the U.S.

The project reps their first teaming behind the scenes in quite some time after they’ve separately made their own movies: Joel with Apple’s The Tragedy of Macbeth starring Denzel Washington and Frances McDormand, and Ethan with the crime comedies Drive-Away Dolls and Honey Don’t! articles.content: EXCLUSIVE: Big UK production groups and studios have been busily preparing for new anti-harassment laws that will impact the film and TV industry, but questions remain. Last Friday, UK-wide legislation came into force that means employers are now liable for harassment of their staff, cast and crew by third parties. Employers must take “all reasonable steps” to prevent harassment, the law now states, and claims can be made up to six months after an incident takes place. The legislation is part of the UK’s much-discussed Employment Rights Act, one of the ruling Labour Paty’s flagship pieces of reform. Watch on Deadline In practice, this change means that if cast or crew are harassed during a production by a third party, be that an agent, someone on location or even someone who has nothing to do with the project, the production company or studio could now be liable for the claim. “This is a significant change,” said Elizabeth Peyton-Jones, who runs The Talent Trust, which takes real-time reaction data from crew working on productions. “As an employer, you can’t now say, ‘I can’t control what other people do.’ You have to take responsibility. articles.title: ‘Jimmy’ Review: KJ Apa Expertly Channels James Stewart In An Inspiring Movie That Tells The Story The Beloved Oscar Winning Star Kept To Himself
articles.content: When Kelly Stewart Harcourt (who is also an Executive Producer) was told about the idea of making a movie about her father, the Oscar winning legend James Stewart , her reaction was that it might be pretty boring since her dad didn’t live a life full of scandals, drugs, drinking or other staples of biopics about movie stars. In other words he was a straight up guy. Then she learned the pitch wasn’t to do a standard birth to death typical film in the genre, but one that focused on the period of his life of which he was most proud, his service in the U.S. military, more specifically World War II where he flew 20 dangerous missions over Europe as a combat pilot in the U.S. Army Air Corps, rising to the title of Colonel at war’s end (and ultimately Brigadier General). It was, she says, something he never spoke about to her or her siblings. Jimmy aims to change all that and bring this largely unpublicized part of Stewart’s life to the frontlines and give it the attention it deserves. The movie doesn’t ignore completely his status as a movie star or his film career but that is just a starting off point. That aspect comes more fully into view at the end of the war with his doubts, even depression, about his ability to return in front of the cameras after director Frank Capra (who previously directed Stewart in You Can’t Take It With You, and Mr. Smith Goes To Washington) worked hard to convince the star to do a script he had, It’s A Wonderful Life. The film is far more effective when focusing on his experiences in the war and post-war dealing with what is now known as PTSD. When he’s trying to find his way and worth back into society — and Hollywood — Jimmy proves to be a cut above your average movie star biopic. Watch on Deadline We do get a sense of the kind of fame Stewart had as the winds of war started to blow. He was a major star, even winning a Best Actor Oscar in early 1941 for The Philadelphia Story after having first been nominated for Mr. Smith the year before.

articles.title: Sharon Horgan’s ‘Youth’ Renewed For Season 2 At HBO
articles.content: Sharon Horgan is returning as literary agent Alex after HBO renewed Youth for a second season. Youth follows a 50-year-old divorcee’s search for sex and love whilst juggling caring for her ailing parents and parenting her should-be grown up son. Horgan stars as Alex in the series, which she created and wrote. [ SPOILER ALERT ] The eight-part season was left open ended after Alex ends it with Patrick, played by Rupert Friend after discovering a list of pros and cons, with the inability to have children as in the latter column. However, after a one-night stand with her nemesis Malcolm, played by Douglas Hodge, she wakes up to find that her boss Sam, played by Sharlene Whyte, has signed Malcolm. All of this while dealing with a UTI and trying to resolve things with her child Ruari, played by Aran Murphy. Robbie Gee also stars as Frank, Sam’s husband. Youth is produced by Horgan’s Merman and she exec produces alongside Faye Dorn, Jim Kleverweis, and Dawn Shadforth, who also directs. Watch on Deadline Youth comes seven years after Horgan’s last HBO show, Divorce , ended after three seasons. Catastrophe co-creator Horgan is also behind Apple black comedy Bad Sisters , Starz’s Courteney Cox-fronted Shining Vale and BBC comedy Motherland . “I’m so happy to get another opportunity to live out my emotional and biological crises on HBO. articles.title: Elena Maganini, Film Editor on ‘Dexter,’ ‘Henry, Portrait of a Serial Killer,’ Dies at 70
articles.content: Elena Maganini, a TV and film editor who won an Emmy for cutting the pilot for “ Dexter ” and edited several films for director John McNaughton, died Oct. 21 in Burbank of complications from breast cancer. She was 70. Born in Chicago, she graduated from the U. of Illinois and studied filmmaking at Columbia College in Chicago. Maganini started out working at Sinnot & Associates, a Chicago production company. Related Stories Original 'Hunger Games' Star Elizabeth Banks Praises ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ as 'Amazing': Joseph Zada Is a 'Perfect' Haymitch Her first feature credit came for McNaughton’s influential 1986 “Henry, Portrait of a Serial Killer.” She went on to edit McNaughton films including “Wild Things,” which starred Matt Dillon, Neve Campbell and Kevin Bacon, “Mad Dog & Glory” and “Sex, Drugs and Rock & Roll,” “The Borrower,” “Speaking of Sex” and “Lansky.” Other feature credits include “Next Friday” and “Ed Gein.” Moving into television, Maganini edited the pilot for “Dexter,” for which she won an Emmy, and went on to edit shows including “Madam Secretary,” “Good Behavior,” “Clarice,” “Manifest” and “The Cleaning Lady.” She was nominated for an Emmy and a Cable ACE Award for “If These Walls Could Talk,” an anthology about abortion directed by Cher and Nancy Savoca and starring Catherine Keener, Demi Moore and Shirley Knight. Survivors include husband Scott Collins, communications director at Motion Picture Editors Guild; daughter Gabriella Coronel; and daughter-in-law Adrienne Coronel. articles.content: A new screenwriting lab in India wants to steer the country’s horror films away from ghost stories and horror-comedy hybrids. Independent outfit Platoon One Films will pick 15 writers for a three-month program built around original genre scripts. The Platoon One Horror Lab will run entirely online, and each of the 15 participants will bring an original horror screenplay to develop. Sessions will take place on weekends and will be led by seasoned screenwriters and directors from India and other countries. The format mixes group mentoring, discussions on craft and individual sessions on each script, so that writers get ongoing feedback as their drafts evolve. The company will name the program’s mentors and faculty in the next few weeks. “We can talk about much bigger, philosophical and metaphysical ideas through horror, and sometimes it is far more powerful than simply expressing them through dialogue,” said Shiladitya Bora , founder of Platoon One Films. “What attracts me to the genre is often the messaging beneath the surface. articles.title: Disney Expected to Lay Off Thousands of Staffers in Biggest Round of Cuts This Year
articles.content: Disney is gearing up for a significant round of layoffs, with some managers told to cut expenses by 20% on an annualized basis, Bloomberg News reported . It would be the fourth round of job cuts in 2026 under Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro and affect the most number of staffers. The Bloomberg report, which cited anonymous sources, said some Disney operations “will be affected disproportionately,” but it did not provide details on which areas would suffer the brunt of the cutbacks. D’Amaro “aims to reinvest a portion of the savings into film and TV programming, technology and the theme parks and cruise ship businesses,” according to the report. Related Stories Original 'Hunger Games' Star Elizabeth Banks Praises ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ as 'Amazing': Joseph Zada Is a 'Perfect' Haymitch Disney has been planning a major restructuring of its TV operations, which would eliminate hundreds of jobs and consolidate divisions, the Wall Street Journal reported last month. In late September, Disney let go a few hundred employees , primarily in its human resources and IT departments across corporate and within different divisions. In July, Disney made job cuts eliminating several hundred jobs across certain corporate functions, including at Pixar, ESPN, Disney Entertainment Television and Disney’s studios. And in April, the Mouse House eliminated about 1,000 roles , primarily as a result of D’Amaro’s formation of a consolidated enterprise marketing division under the leadership of Asad Ayaz, chief marketing and brand officer. Dana Walden, Disney’s president and chief creative officer, addressed the most recent Disney layoffs at the Bloomberg Screentime event last month. “I think, like all of our similarly situated competitors, and certainly all of our competitors in the tech industry, there is a need to constantly evaluate how you’re structured,” Walden said. In August, Disney offered early-retirement buyout packages to longtime executives, as part of its ongoing cost-cutting efforts.

articles.content: Cynthia Nixon is standing by her “Sex and the City” character Miranda Hobbes’ arc in the chaotic reboot “ And Just Like That ” — despite how bewildering some fans found it. In a recent interview with The New York Times , the actress explained that despite the fact that the show’s viewers “were so horrified by [Miranda’s] sadness and alcoholism and awkwardness at trying to become a woke person at this advanced age,” that was what she appreciated most about the character. “I loved that,” she said. Related Stories Original 'Hunger Games' Star Elizabeth Banks Praises ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ as 'Amazing': Joseph Zada Is a 'Perfect' Haymitch While Hobbes underwent several personal shifts in the reboot of the iconic 6 Season HBO drama, the most contentious point for audiences was her relationship with comedian Che Diaz , whom she left her husband, Steve Brady, for in Season 1. In the original series, Hobbes, a lawyer, met Brady, a bartender, in Season 2, then broke up, ultimately got back together, got married, and welcomed a child, Brady Hobbes, by the show’s end. Nixon also spoke of how she was swayed to reprise the role of Hobbes in the reboot to begin with. “I became convinced that we could really do interesting, dangerous things,” she said. “And that we could make up for some of our past mistakes, the chief one being that it was such an overwhelmingly white show.” And while reactions to the show were always a mixed bag, Nixon admits she was caught off guard when she learned “And Just Like That” wouldn’t be returning for a fourth season: “I was not at all ready,” she said. “Not at all.” Currently, Nixon stars in HBO’s historical drama “The Gilded Age” as Ada Forte. The show debuted in Jan. 2022 and has run for three subsequent seasons. Season 4 premiered on Sunday on HBO and HBO Max. Despite the success of “The Gilded Age,” though, Nixon noted that “Miranda seems to eclipse everything else” she’s done, even 22 years after “Sex and the City” finished airing in 2004.

articles.title: HBO Renews Sharon Horgan Comedy ‘Youth’ For a Season 2
articles.content: HBO has given a Season 2 order to “ Youth ,” the latest series from Peabody and BAFTA winner Sharon Horgan . The series’ Season 1 is currently streaming on HBO Max. In the show, Horgan plays a 50-year-old divorcee navigating relationships, her ailing parents and her troubled son, who isn’t quite gelling at his new college. articles.content: Club Kid , Jordan Firstman ’s acclaimed film about a club promoter who stays too long at the party, has been submitted by distributor A24 for Golden Globes consideration as a drama, rather than a musical/comedy, The Hollywood Reporter has exclusively learned. This classification means that the film — which Firstman wrote, directed (as his feature directorial debut) and stars in — will compete in the genre-specific Globes categories (picture, actor and actress) against the likes of The Odyssey , La Bola Negra , Dune: Part Three , Elsinore , All of a Sudden , Fjord and Possible Love , rather than Wild Horse Nine , The Invite , The Debut , Artificial , Obsession , Project Hail Mary and Tender Loving Care . Related Stories General News 2026 Daytime Emmy Awards: 'General Hospital' Wins Best Daytime Drama TV The Hollywood Reporter Wins 2026 Daytime Emmy Award A24’s decision, which was made in close consultation with Firstman, may come as a surprise to some given Firstman’s background in comedy and the fact that some have described Club Kid as an elevated variation of Big Daddy , the 1999 Adam Sandler comedy about a man who unexpectedly becomes the guardian of a young child. But Club Kid becomes considerably more dramatic as it progresses, and Firstman — who shines in a decidedly dramatic courtroom scene late in the film — has cited heavier films like 1978’s An Unmarried Woman and 1979’s Kramer vs. Kramer as key inspirations. Club Kid had its world premiere at the Cannes Film Festival in the Un Certain Regard section, after which it received a seven-minute standing ovation and sparked an overnight bidding war among distributors. The film ultimately sold to A24 for $17 million, making it the biggest sale of the fest. It has since played to raves at the Telluride, Toronto, New York and other film fests. articles.summary: The new gig is a reunion for ThankYouX and Powell: During the latter's run at Paramount Pictures, he painted of portrait of Steve Jobs for her office on the lot.
articles.content: The company has tapped Wilson — best known by his professional moniker ThankYouX — to serve as its first artist in residence. The unique appointment, confirmed today by Vice Studios president Amy Powell , will find Wilson collaborating with development and creative teams on a variety of functions. He’ll be charged with originating new intellectual property, consulting on visual world-building for Vice Studios titles and conceptualize hybrid narrative formats that “bridge contemporary art, entertainment and technology,” per Vice. articles.title: Tallinn Black Nights Fest Turns 30 With New Artistic Director, a Latin American Streak and a Baltic Boom

articles.content: Estonia’s Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ) is kicking off its 30th edition on Friday, the first under the creative leadership of artistic director Triin Tramberg . The lineup promises a mix of new discoveries and gems, envelope-pushing films and the best of the year’s festival circuit. The film curator, whose profile has grown alongside PÖFF’s over more than 15 years, began her work at the fest as a program assistant before becoming a program coordinator and playing a key role in shaping Tallinn’s international profile. PÖFF founder and longtime fest director Tiina Lokk , who remains CEO, has shifted her focus to overall strategic and developmental direction. articles.title: ‘You Can See Everything,’ ‘Clayface’ Fighting for No. 1 in Quiet Halloween Weekend
articles.summary: The Elizabeth Holmes documentary could land the first No. 1 of its buzzy three-week run as the studios avoided major releases over the spooky frame.
articles.content: A24’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything , which includes a memorable discussion about the classic comedy routine “Who’s on First,” sparked questions about whether the movie itself could take first place over Clayface as the two films battled at the box office during a subdued Halloween weekend. Sunday figures show the two movies still neck and neck for the top spot domestically, with directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim ‘s You Can See Everything looking like the early winner at $10.6 million in its third weekend to bring its North American cume to $63.8 million. Currently playing in 3,243 North American locations, the Oscar-buzzed documentary eyes its first No. 1 finish. It looks to decline around 43 percent for the weekend that saw the studios avoid releasing new titles as Halloween fell on a Saturday. If this holds, the three-hour You Can See Everything would follow previous features True Grit , Argo and 1917 as films that hit No. 1 in their third frames. Despite the meager overall turnout for this weekend’s moviegoing, the domestic box office’s 2026 take of $8.46 billion still puts it around 20 percent ahead of last year’s total sum to this point, according to Rentrak. Just behind You Can See Everything for the time being is Clayface , as filmmaker James Watkins’ body horror feature looks to gross around $10.4 million in its sophomore frame for a two-week North American sum of $44.1 million. Tom Rhys Harries and Naomi Ackie star in the $44 million-budgeted Warner Bros. release that marks DC Studios ‘ third theatrical title for bosses James Gunn and Peter Safran after 2025’s Superman and this summer’s underperforming Supergirl . Clayface looks to decline around 56 percent for the weekend from 3,478 domestic theaters. The sold-out shows easily drew the liveliest crowds of this year’s Tokyo festival — the latest Toho -backed monster epic doesn’t open commercially in Japan until Nov. 3 — with numerous die-hard kaiju fans attending in costume or carrying their own Gojira figurines into the theater. articles.summary: "I still see him, but he is fine," the 'Basic Instinct' actor said of the three-time Oscar winner who has stayed out of the spotlight in recent years.
articles.content: Michael Douglas is sharing a rare update on Jack Nicholson , who has largely remained out of the spotlight in recent years. During an appearance to promote his memoir One Helluva Ride in Swansea, the Basic Instinct actor was asked about his relationship with Nicholson. “I would have liked to have acted with Jack,” Douglas said, per The Independent . “He’s not working any more. He’s well. He has disappeared. I know that.” He added, “I still see him, but he is fine. He is up there by his house and walking around in his slippers. It happens. He deserves it. I understand. He is a few years older than me, but I understand.” Related Stories Movies Ray Nicholson Levels Up With 'The Mosquito Bowl': "I'm Always Battling for Legitimacy" Movies Michael Douglas Memoir's 7 Wildest Revelations: Secret Co-Star Affairs to Coke Binges Douglas is 82, and Nicholson is 89. The two actors only professionally collaborated on 1975’s One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest , which Douglas produced and Nicholson starred in. Nicholson’s most recent movie, How Do You Know , came out in 2010 and also starred Reese Witherspoon, Paul Rudd and Owen Wilson. One of Nicholson’s last public appearances was in February 2025 at the Saturday Night Live 50th anniversary special. A month before that, his daughter, Lorraine Nicholson, shared a photo with her father on Instagram. Also through Lorraine’s social media, she shared a photo of the three-time Oscar winner on her Instagram Story in April to commemorate his 89th birthday. Douglas’ press tour for his memoir has been headline-making. He revealed in a bombshell excerpt from One Helluva Ride that he and Kathleen Turner had a secret romantic relationship while filming 1984’s Romancing the Stone . Responding to Douglas’ admission, the actress told People , “Good heavens what a fuss about something 40 years ago! I love Michael and I look forward to enjoying the book.”

articles.title: A Royal Surprise: ‘The Remarried Empress’ Releases One Day Early on Disney+ and Hulu
articles.summary: The wildly anticipated Korean fantasy romance, starring Shin Min-a, Ju Ji-hoon, Lee Jong-suk and Lee Se-young, will launch with four episodes Nov. 3, followed by two new installments every Wednesday.
articles.content: In a surprise gift to fans, Disney + and Hulu are moving up the royal arrival of The Remarried Empress , bringing the lavish Korean fantasy romance to viewers Nov. 3, one day ahead of its previously announced premiere. Stars Shin Min-a, Ju Ji-hoon, Lee Jong-suk and Lee Se-young revealed the change Tuesday at a press conference in Seoul. The first four episodes will be available at launch, with Disney describing the early release as a thank you to fans for their support. The rest of the 10-episode series’ rollout remains unchanged: Two new episodes will arrive each Wednesday beginning Nov. 11, with the final pair streaming Nov. 25. Related Stories TV Disney Night Returns on 'Dancing With the Stars' With a Broadway Twist: See the Scores, Who Went Home (Updating Live) Lifestyle Designer Rebecca Minkoff Drafts Model and Reality TV Star Grace Ann Nader for Capsule Collection Based on the hit Naver Webtoon, The Remarried Empress combines palace intrigue, romantic betrayal and an impossibly elegant heroine determined to claim her own future. Shin plays Navier, the empress of the Eastern Empire, whose marriage unravels when her husband, Emperor Sovieshu (Ju), falls for escaped slave girl Rashta (Lee Se-young). Navier agrees to his request for a divorce on one condition: She must be permitted to marry her own budding love — Crown Prince Heinrey (Lee Jong-suk) of the rival Western Kingdom. The series was adapted for the screen by Yeoh Geena and Hyun Choongyeol and directed by Cho Suwon, whose credits include Still 17 and Pinocchio . The early premiere announcement follows the series’ sold-out preview screenings at the Busan International Film Festival in October. According to Disney, the show’s trailer generated more than 13 million views across YouTube and social media platforms in its first 48 hours, while the wildly popular original webtoon on which the show is based has amassed nearly three billion views.

articles.content: Imagine Entertainment and Weed Road are developing a series based on the 2011 book by Daniel H. Spielberg flirted with the book for years, with Anne Hathaway and Chris Hemsworth attached to star. Spielberg eventually postponed the project indefinitely in 2014, with Michael Bay coming aboard in 2018 to direct . That version didn’t get made either. Wilbon noted that he is diabetic, saying that “The bill has come due from too many red eye flights and just the stuff that I had ignored. articles.content: Series’ Women , the European female leadership program organized by the Erich Pommer Institut (EPI), has unveiled the 15 female producers from 12 countries that it has selected for its sixth edition. Launched in 2021, the initiative “supports female producers in advancing their careers, strengthening their professional networks and increasing the visibility of female-driven projects across the European screen industry,” EPI says. The program combines expert-led training in visibility, leadership and digital entrepreneurship with individual mentoring and pitching coaching tailored to participants’ career goals. Exclusive networking opportunities at major European industry markets also provide direct access to key industry players and foster lasting connections. The goal is to strengthen female leadership, promote the professional development of women producers and contribute to greater diversity and representation across the European screen industry. Among the major networking opportunities are TV Drama Vision, presented by the Göteborg Film Festival in Sweden, and Series Mania Forum in Lille, France. Through an online diversity training course designed for hiring managers or decision-makers at the producers’ companies, Series’ Women also looks to address topics of gender equality and diversity at an organizational level. articles.summary: "I'll go to work with [Jerry] Bruckheimer tomorrow for anything," the "Ebenezer" star says The post Johnny Depp Wants to End ‘Pirates of the Caribbean’ Franchise ‘On a Better Note’ appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: “I’ll go to work with [Jerry] Bruckheimer tomorrow for anything,” the “Ebenezer” star says The “Alice in Wonderland” star talked to Entertainment Tonight as part of the press tour for “Ebenezer,” a return to the spotlight after Depp’s highly publicized legal saga with Amber Heard involving claims of domestic violence and defamation. In the interview, Depp said that he would be willing to return to his Oscar-nominated role of Jack Sparrow in a long-discussed sixth “Pirates of the Caribbean” movie. “If things are exactly where they need to be with regards to how they’re going to top off the ‘Pirates,’ the only involvement that I really want to have, truly, is just to send them off on a better note,” Depp told the outlet. Depp isn’t wrong that the series left off on a sour note. The fourth film in the franchise, “Pirates of the Caribbean: On Stranger Tides,” and the fifth, “Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales,” were both critically panned in comparison to the first trilogy of films. While “On Stranger Tides” was the franchise’s second-highest grossing entry with a $1.045 billion haul, “Dead Men Tell No Tales” was the second-lowest, bringing home roughly $795 million (still a high sum). After debuting as Jack Sparrow in 2003’s “Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl,” Depp said he would be willing to return for any sequel so long as producer Jerry Bruckheimer is involved. “I’ll go to work with Bruckheimer tomorrow for anything,” he said. “Doesn’t matter, if it’s Jerry. I trust him, and we have deep friendship.”

articles.title: Martin McDonagh Reevaluates His Use of N-Word, Racist Language in Prior Works: ‘My Heart Was in the Right Place’
articles.summary: The "Wild Horse Nine" filmmaker says political correctness has "gotten worse, especially in the last 10 years" The post Martin McDonagh Reevaluates His Use of N-Word, Racist Language in Prior Works: ‘My Heart Was in the Right Place’ appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: The “Wild Horse Nine” filmmaker says political correctness has “gotten worse, especially in the last 10 years” Martin McDonagh took a closer look at past use of racist language in his work while speaking with the New York Times on Saturday, saying that slurs like the N-word have been used “to be either outrageous or to be truthful” and that his “heart was in the right place” when he wrote such material. Sitting with the filmmaker and playwright for the Times’ “The Interview” podcast , co-host David Marchese asked McDonagh if past criticisms of his brash language have inspired him to change his approach to writing — and more pointedly, if he thought the barometer of acceptability with such language has changed with shifting expectations of political correctness. “I think it’s gotten worse, especially in the last 10 years,” McDonagh said of those expectations. “Only in the last 10 years have I been asked to change words in place from 25, 30 years ago because of offense taken by certain words that weren’t there 25 years ago. And my approach to it is that those words were there to be either outrageous or to be truthful. If you’re writing a, for instance, racist character, they’re going to use racist language. To try and cut those out 25 years later — for what reason? I’m never quite sure. “It feels not just problematic, but it feels like things are getting troublingly worse about that because I was never asked to do that back in the day. And I think if you don’t like that in a play, you should just not do the play. You shouldn’t try and change the play 25 years later.” McDonagh was then asked about specific criticisms of his 2010 play “A Behanding in Spokane” and 2017’s Searchlight feature “Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri,” which in the case of the former some have said portrays a Black character as a Stepin Fetchit type and in the latter a racist as a redeemable hero . articles.summary: "One of the candidates showed up as she promised, and the other did not," Dustin Lance Black writes The post ‘Milk’ Oscar Winner Calls Nithya Raman ‘Not a Dependable Politician’ in Surprise Switch to Karen Bass appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: “One of the candidates showed up as she promised, and the other did not,” Dustin Lance Black writes Dustin Lance Black, an Oscar-winning screenwriter best known for the 2008 biopic “Milk,” pulled his endorsement for L.A. Mayoral candidate Nithya Raman after she was an alleged “no show” at a fundraising event he held for her. On Sunday, the Oscar winner took to Instagram and uploaded a video explaining why he was now endorsing incumbent Mayor Karen Bass. “They are both exception people, but I gotta say, with the challenges ahead, I think the most important thing to do is to have experience and to show up,” Black said. “One of the candidates showed up as she promised, and the other did not. And so, I’m going to be voting for Karen Bass for mayor of Los Angeles.” Black reportedly hosted a campaign fundraiser, called “A Reception with Nithya Raman,” for Raman back in October. However, as Black claimed in the comments of his upload, Raman never made it to the event. While responding to actor Paul Scheer, who appeared to voice concerns about Bass’ dedication to Hollywood , Black noted he had “other issues” with Raman, but specifically called out her “no show” status at his fundraising event. “Among other issues, Raman was a no show to an event she personally reached out and asked us to hold for her,” he wrote. “Her staff then lied about the reasons why she vanished—with no heads up. If this were unique to us I would have taken the knock. But in conversations with other previous Raman supporters I discovered this is Raman’s way.” He added: “I too had been a supporter, but it turns out she is not a dependable politician. Unfortunately. Not the kind of change that is going to help this city we both love, Paul.” A representative for Raman did not immediately respond to TheWrap’s request for comment. articles.summary: Lulu Wilson has Regina George's snark and Jason Voorhees' homicidal mania in the latest wildly entertaining, absurdly violent "Becky" sequel The post ‘The Last Temptation of Becky’ Review: This Badass Antifa Franchise Deserves a Bigger Budget appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: Lulu Wilson has Regina George’s snark and Jason Voorhees’ homicidal mania in the latest wildly entertaining, absurdly violent “Becky” sequel The older you get, the more you realize life is about the simple pleasures. An uninterrupted, full night of sleep. A tall glass of iced tea on a hot summer’s day. An introductory paragraph that seamlessly transitions into an amusing tonal shift. Lulu Wilson decapitating Nazis. Stuff like that. Lulu Wilson has turned killing white supremacists into a cottage industry, and in the “Becky” movies, business is booming. In the original “Becky” (2020), she slaughtered escaped neo-Nazi convicts led by a surprisingly sinister Kevin James. In “The Wrath of Becky” (2023), she laid a one-woman siege against the not-quite-Proud Boys, led by a surprisingly sinister Seann William Scott. “Becky” was great, “The Wrath of Becky” was even better, and now “The Last Temptation of Becky” pits her against a predictably sinister Neil Patrick Harris as a Nazi mad scientist with a scheme to take over the world. The new film is, like the previous installments, a glorious Antifa power fantasy in an era when fascists are increasingly comfortable poking their heads out from the sewage pile of history (where they belong). Jenn Wexler’s film, co-written by Matt Angel, moves the “Becky” franchise from low-budget grindhouse territory into the superspy genre, and it’s as ecstatically entertaining as ever. The only downside is that “The Last Temptation of Becky’s” ambitions aren’t matched by its budget. The genre shift makes sense. James Bond killed oodles of billionaires, and audiences pumped their fists in triumph. Becky kills white supremacists, and we do the same — except Becky does her job without Bond’s raging misogyny and repeated sexual assaults. So while these “Becky” films lack the Bond franchise’s spectacle, in some ways they’re more satisfying overall. articles.title: ‘Okinawa Saudade’ Review: A Moving Documentary About the Okinawan-Brazilian Community Explores the History of Displacement
articles.summary: Yoju Matsubayashi's latest film follows third-generation Okinawan-Brazilian as they reflect on their distant homeland.
articles.content: The Kasato Maru ferried 325 Okinawans to Brazil in 1908, making it the first immigrant ship from Japan to do so. That history is highlighted by the opening of the documentary “ Okinawa Saudade ,” (“saudade” being a Portuguese word for bittersweet longing, typically around a memory or place). The film looks at the results a century later, now that an estimated 200,000 Brazilians of Okinawan descent are living in Brazil today, and director and cinematographer Yoju Matsubayashi finds a specific and emotionally straightforward route into complicated history. The director has covered the subject to some extent before in 2020’s “Okinawa / Santos,” a film which collected testimony on the forced deportation and even internment of Japanese immigrants in Brazil in the 1940s.””Okinawa Saudade”” narrows that focus to the families of two third-generation Okinawan-Brazilians, specifically ones with an interest in — and a longing towards — the island their families came from, something partially explored through the arts. articles.title: AT&T and IndieWire’s Filmmaker Party at AFI Fest Celebrated Filmmakers and Those Who Champion Them
articles.summary: A week after partnering on our Future of Filmmaking Summit, AT&T and IndieWire teamed up again to celebrate the next generation of storytellers.
articles.content: IndieWire and AT&T spent the month of October demonstrating our shared commitment to championing filmmakers and bringing untold stories to life. First up was the IndieWire Future of Filmmaking Summit in Los Angeles, presented by AT&T, which assembled artists, executives, and thought leaders from every corner of the entertainment industry for a day of programming about where Hollywood is heading. Then a week later, we partnered to present the Filmmaker Party at AFI Fest , which celebrated the next generation of filmmakers who are bringing their visions to life. Held at Ovation Hollywood on Saturday, October 25, the Filmmaker Party brought directors and festival attendees together for an evening of networking and movie discussions. The party even featured a complimentary headshot booth for anyone who wanted to take their career to the next level. That the movie took place before Ishirō Honda’s original “Godzilla,” and 2.) articles.title: ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Will Be in 3D in Theaters — and on Meta’s New VR Glasses
articles.summary: Lionsgate is partnering with Facebook parent company Meta on the 3D version of the film and will collaborate on future titles for the VR glasses hitting shelves next spring.
articles.content: Lionsgate ‘s “Hunger Games” prequel “ The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping ” will be available in 3D when it opens in theaters on November 20. That on its own isn’t strictly news, but the 3D conversion on the film is coming from a new and unlikely place: Facebook parent company Meta . Meta is partnering with Lionsgate to convert “Sunrise on the Reaping” to 3D, with director Francis Lawrence working to adapt the film for 3D viewing. Meta worked with VFX giant DNEG and their internal 3D conversion branch Stereo. This is the first time Meta has partnered with a Hollywood film studio on such an undertaking, and it also won’t be the last Lionsgate movie that will get the 3D treatment down the road (other titles will be announced at a later date). Related Stories ‘Mouse’ Review: ‘Saint Frances’ and ‘Ghostlight’ Filmmakers Bring Their Singular Humanity to a Coming-of-Age Tale ‘I Play Rocky’ Review: Sylvester Stallone’s Wild Hollywood Underdog Story Gets a Punchy Crowdpleaser In addition to “Sunrise on the Reaping” being in 3D in theaters, the movie will eventually be available on Meta VR Glasses when those VR devices hit the shelves in spring 2027. IndieWire got to demo those recently, and they’re designed to be lighter and less obtrusive than other VR headsets that can be tougher on the eyes while not sacrificing any of the immersive qualities (they feel and look like slightly larger sunglasses that you might get at the dentist rather than a bulky, wraparound headset that weighs on your face). articles.title: ‘Mouse’ Review: ‘Saint Frances’ and ‘Ghostlight’ Filmmakers Bring Their Singular Humanity to a Coming-of-Age Tale
articles.summary: Around these parts, every Kelly O'Sullivan and Alex Thompson feature film is an event. The pair's third production together is no exception — and their best to date.
articles.content: [Editor’s note: This review was originally published on February 13, 2026 at the 2026 Berlin Film Festival. IFC Films will release it in select theaters on Friday, November 6.] For the final 20 or so minutes of an early screening of Kelly O’Sullivan and Alex Thompson ‘s Berlin-bound “ Mouse ” that I recently attended, the woman sitting behind me in one of NYC’s smallest screening rooms sobbed. Like, really sobbed. I could hear her gasps in between her cries. Yes, I thought to myself, one of my people . While I’m not sure there’s yet a cult assembled around the deeply empathetic and uniquely humane cinema of O’Sullivan and Thompson (partners in both film and life), God willing, there will be after more audiences see the pair’s third effort. I’ve been banging the drum on their wondrous output since 2020’s “Saint Frances” ( which Thompson directed and O’Sullivan wrote and starred in ) and their deep-feeling follow-up, 2024’s “Ghostlight” (written by O’Sullivan, who also joined Thompson in co-directing duties). Around these parts, any O’Sullivan and Thompson joint is an event . articles.summary: Peter Farrelly continues his reign of making audience-delighting hits for the TIFF crowd, but this one pulls its punches a bit.
articles.content: [Editor’s note: This review was originally published on September 13, 2026 at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival. Amazon MGM Studios will release it in select theaters on Friday, November 6, before going wide on Friday, November 20.] You’re going to see the hits coming with this one. When Anthony Ippolito first utters the title of Peter Farrelly ‘s “ I Play Rocky ” — it’s an admission and an ask, a demand and a plea — the moment is primed for stand-up-and-cheer crowd-pleasing. Such is the case with Farrelly’s entire film , which tracks Sylvester Stallone’s wild, improbable Hollywood success story through the lens of his creation of “Rocky,” often functioning as its own version of that underdog story, presumably because “Rocky” proper isn’t available to be remade and Stallone was not formally involved with the production of this one. The guy sold his dog when he didn’t have enough money! But Peter Gamble’s script sands down those hard edges into something much more made-for-the-movies, a distinctly knotty treatment for a movie that is meant to be about how hard it is to get original movies made. While the lightness of the film — including an awkward dinner in which Frank Stallone, Jr. (Matt Dillon) giddily admits to beating his kid, mostly played for chuckles — can detract from the much darker stuff that really happened to Stallone, it’s hard to deny the power of a feature so genuinely built to delight. articles.title: IndieWire’s Trevor Wallace Wins Daytime Emmy for Editing ‘IndieWire Craft Roundtables’
articles.summary: IndieWire's long-time video producer won for editing the first season of our PBS series.
articles.content: Wallace won the Editing for a Daytime Studio Program category at the 53rd annual Daytime Emmys for his work on Season 1 of “IndieWire Craft Roundtables .” He accepted the award during the ceremony at the Hollywood Palladium on Friday, October 30. IndieWire was also nominated for a Daytime Emmy for Outstanding Directing for a Daytime Studio Non-Fiction Series for IndieWire executive producer Mary Pelloni’s work on the show. The two nominations and one win, in categories that also included broadcast talk shows, reflect IndieWire’s increasing presence in the traditional video spaces in addition to our written coverage. Related Stories ‘The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins’ Is the Funniest Series of the Year Netflix Will Give Joel Coen’s Gothic Mystery ‘Jack of Spades’ a Theatrical Release in 2027 Wallace works on IndieWire’s staff as a video producer, where he also produces and edits video content across brands like Filmmaker Toolkit, Future of Filmmaking, and other editorial and sponsored projects. Season 1 of “IndieWire Craft Roundtables” highlighted the below-the-line artisans on many of the biggest films of the season. Hosted by IndieWire’s Jim Hemphill, the season consisted of four episodes, each centered around a different filmmaking department: cinematography, editing, production design, and casting. Each episode aired on PBS SoCal and streamed on the PBS App in addition to editorial coverage on IndieWire.com. Wallace won for the editing roundtable episode, which featured included editors Kirk Baxter (“A House of Dynamite”), Affonso Goncalves (“Hamnet”), Michael P. Shawver (“Sinners”), Andy Jurgensen (“One Battle After Another”), Pamela Martin (“Springsteen: Deliver Me from Nowhere”), Saar Klein (“Dead Man’s Wire”), and Luke Lynch (“BLKNWS: Terms & Conditions”). The cinematography roundtable featured Adolpho Veloso (“Train Dreams”), Malik Hassan Sayeed (“After the Hunt”), Michael Bauman (“One Battle After Another”), and William Rexer (“The Testament of Ann Lee”).
